title: Transformer-assisted bibliometric analysis maps changes in Italian computer science
summary: A study combined learned co-authorship and text representations with topic clustering to analyze a roster of 1,229 Italian computer-science scholars and publication records from 1980–2025. It identified three model-derived periods spanning foundational work, computer vision/machine learning, and later applied AI/health informatics. An ancillary Genoa pilot introduced 15 recommended researcher pairs, with four joint projects reported within six months. The topic patterns depend on metadata and analytical thresholds, 44.2% of paper abstracts were missing, and the small uncontrolled pilot does not establish a causal collaboration benefit.
ai_technology: Node2vec, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence transformer, BERTopic/HDBSCAN, Falcon and Gemini topic-label generation

evidence.tested: The framework models 1,229 Italian CS scholars. Forecast backtesting trained on 2010–2020 and tested on 2021–2023 for 130 authors and 6,084 forecasts (reported SES MAE 7.75 vs. moving-average 8.08). In the University of Genoa pilot, 15 system-flagged researcher pairs were introduced at a showcase; the authors report four started joint projects within six months.
evidence.unknown: Generalization beyond this national disciplinary population, metadata/disambiguation bias and model-dependent topic labels remain limitations. The15-pair pilot lacks a controlled comparator; a locked model and pre-specified prospective evaluation protocol are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Graph and transformer representations are combined to identify semantic similarity and temporal topics; this enables the reported field-evolution patterns and candidate collaboration recommendations, with LLMs used to label discovered topics.

source_review.scope: Original PLOS full text: source population/metadata gaps, learned embeddings/topic modeling, longitudinal patterns, backtesting, ancillary collaboration pilot, affiliations and date.
